newsitem.title: GERMANY: Hugo Boss seeks to sell U.S. unit.
newsitem.headline: Hugo Boss seeks to sell U.S. unit.

text.p: German clothes manufacturer Hugo Boss AG said on Friday it was looking to dispose of its New York-based U.S. unit The Joseph & Feiss Company.
Boss, which said it had not determined how the disposal would take place, said that in any case "the measure would likely not affect its 1996 group result negatively".

Hugo Boss said that if no buyer for the business could be found, some 280 workers faced redundancy at the Cleveland, Ohio-based TJFC group, which makes Joseph & Feiss brands including Cricketeer and Country Britches.
Workers there who were involved in production for its Hugo Boss Fashions unit would, however, continue to be employed.
Hugo Boss said it had taken the decision as a result of the tough conditions and competition in the mid-price clothing range and the limited outlook for improvement.
The German premium clothes-maker bought the U.S. unit in 1989. Last year it had a turnover of 53.3 million marks.
